speaker: paulsuiter
text: That would be me, Your Worship. Director of Community Services, good evening, Your Worship, members of Council. Subject tonight is the Clearwater Cemetery Study, and the recommendation the administration will be making this evening is that Council receive and accept the Clearwater Cemetery Study for information purposes at this time. I also have Mr. Grant Tolley. I'm not sure if he's in the waiting room still, but Ms. Winter can bring him in when need be. He's on. Okay, I can't see him there. That's great. So the background on this, going back to 2016, Beaumont District Heritage Society had submitted a request for some funds in order to do an upgrade at the Clearwater Cemetery. I believe the funds were secured based on a matching grant, which they were not able to get. So in 2017, the budget was passed for the $30,000, and has been sitting in a reserve carried forward each budget year. Then in 2018, a decision was made to change the scope of what those funds were for, and they wanted to do a comprehensive study of the Clearwater Cemetery as a strategic document for not only today, for operations as well as for the future. So that study has been completed, and that's what we're here this evening with. The study provides a comprehensive picture of the creation, ownership, usage, and development of the cemetery in order that the value to the city and the surrounding region as a significant historical resource is understood. The study details current functions and planning options for future expansion. The study makes seven recommendations, which cover maintenance operations, future planning options for growth. Each of these recommendations are sufficiently detailed to assist administration in taking short-term action as well as aid in future budgetary and planning exercises. The seven recommendations, number one would be to prepare historical treaties, conduct additional research. Number two, actions to identify and protect the historic portion and erect interpretive signage. Number three, review of the access to the cemetery as a risk mitigation exercise. Number four would be to increase parking at the site. Number five would be planning to address future expansion. Six, review of the landscape to enhance beautification, and seven, update maintenance plans. This report will provide strategic direction required to address immediate and longer-term concerns for the operation of the cemetery, and administration will work from this study in both the short-term and long-term goals. It also ties back to the strategic pillar of livability, as well as our place to play recreation parks and facilities master plan service delivery, which identifies the need for the cemetery study and future growth planning. So any questions that council would have of Amin or Mr. Tolley, we'd be happy to answer. Thank you.
